thread:
sam_customer: Hey team — our embeddings calls suddenly started returning 384-dim vectors today (we expect 512). No code changes on our side, but we did flip on a quantization flag (int8) last week. Also seeing throughput drop and spikes in tail latency. Anyone seen this?

alice_support: Hi @sam_customer, sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the exact request (headers + body) you used and one example response? Also any correlation_id from the response headers would help.

sam_customer: sure — here’s the curl we used (token redacted):

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  -d '{"model":"embed-xlarge","inputs":["hello world"],"quantization_profile":"int8","batch_size":8}'
```

response (trimmed):

```
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.0012, -0.0034, ...], "dimensions":384}], "meta":{"request_id":"req_9f2b3"}}
```

sam_customer: We also see 400-600ms p95 for single-item calls vs ~120ms baseline before the flag.

alice_support: Thanks. @jordan_ml can you look — model routing/aliasing for quantized variants? Might be selecting a different artifact.

jordan_ml: looking. Quick notes: quantization_profile is supposed to pick a quantized artifact but should NOT change embedding dims. Two possibilities: 1) model alias mapped to a "lite" artifact that uses a different projection head (bad), or 2) we have a serialization mismatch where client receives a trimmed vector (e.g., truncation bug). Asking infra for logs for req_9f2b3. @mike_infra can you grep the loader logs?

mike_infra: pulled logs for req_9f2b3 — I see the following at model load:

```
[2026-03-15 14:12:33] INFO load: model=embed-xlarge-lite-int8 artifact_id=art_8b2a 
[2026-03-15 14:12:33] INFO runtime: kv_cache size=1.2GB workers=4
[2026-03-15 14:12:34] WARN projection_head: dims=384 (expected 512)
```

mike_infra: So the runtime actually loaded a "-lite-int8" artifact that advertises 384 dims.

sam_customer: Wait — we explicitly passed model:add embed-xlarge and quantization=int8. We expected embed-xlarge-int8 with 512 dims. Are there two different int8 artifacts?

jordan_ml: Right now we have two int8 artifacts: embed-xlarge-int8 (full projection head, 512 dims) and embed-xlarge-lite-int8 (memory-optimized, 384 dims). We recently introduced the lite variant for constrained Dedicated nodes. The bug is that alias resolution for the API can resolve to the lite variant when quantization_profile=int8 + routing policy=cost_saver. That should never happen for the hosted API unless the customer is on a tier that requested the lite artifact.

alice_support: So this is an alias/routing policy regression that caused customers to be routed to the lite artifact and thus get 384-d vectors. That explains the dim mismatch. Any idea why latency got worse?

jordan_ml: Two reasons: the lite artifact uses a different kernel path in our runtime with suboptimal f32 fallback in the int8 path; second, batching behavior changed — the lite artifact's batching threshold is different, causing small batches to be processed less efficiently.

sam_customer: Ugh. This breaks a lot of downstream pipelines — they assume 512 dims and feed vectors into our PCA/FAISS index. We've been getting noisy matches.

alice_support: Apologies. Next steps: 1) immediate mitigation: pass model=\"embed-xlarge-int8\" explicit artifact alias or set quantization_profile=\"fp16\" until fixed. 2) engineering to fix alias mapping to avoid routing to lite unless customer's account explicitly allows it. 3) add server-side validation: if returned dims != model_expected_dims => return 409 with informative error.

jordan_ml: Agreed. I'll open ENG-EMBED-457. Quick repro for us: run internal bench tool with --model embed-xlarge --quant int8 and set routing_policy=cost_saver to reproduce. Example: 

```
./bench_embed --model embed-xlarge --quant int8 --routing_policy cost_saver --batch 1 --input tests/short.txt
# should produce artifact=embed-xlarge-lite-int8 and dims=384
```

mike_infra: I've rolled a hotfix to disable cost_saver routing for quantized artifacts on hosted cluster-1. Will monitor p95.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-1234 - "embed routing -> lite-artifact for int8 causing dim mismatch" assigned to jordan_ml, priority=high

sam_customer: Thanks. If you can restore 512-d behavior ASAP that would be great. Meanwhile can you confirm whether fp16 keeps dims at 512?

jordan_ml: fp16 uses the full artifact by default — embed-xlarge-fp16 maps to embed-xlarge-fp16 artifact (512 dims). So a short-term workaround is use quantization_profile: "fp16" or pass explicit model alias embed-xlarge-int8.

alice_support: Action items summarized: 
- jordan_ml: ENG-EMBED-457 open, fix alias resolution + add artifact compatibility checks (due EOD).
- mike_infra: monitor hotfix, rollback if regressions.
- support: notify affected customers and provide workaround (explicit artifact alias or fp16).

sam_customer: Appreciated. One request — can we surface mismatch in client SDKs too (throw if dims != expected)? This would have saved us time.

jordan_ml: +1. I'll add a note to the ticket to add client-side validation in SDKs and to return clearer API error when a routing decision would change dims.

alice_support: Replied to customer email thread with mitigation steps and ETA. Keeping thread open. :thumbsup:

sam_customer: Confirmed workaround works (explicit model alias). dims back to 512 and downstream pipeline is green. Thanks all. :party_popper:
